To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the electron and gamma background in three CRESST detectors, that we have found a 3.64 keV X -ray line from the decay 41 Ca, that we have determined the activity of the 41 Ca line and that we have found that the 40 Ca line is at 3.15 keV.
the electron and gamma background in the energy range 1–100 keV is dominated by a 3.5 keV X-rays from the decay of primordial 41 Ca in the crystal, and by the 2.6 kev X-rays from the 40 K decay.
the electron and gamma background in our detectors is dominated by 40 K, 42 Ca, and 208 Tl, with contributions from cosmogenic activation products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the understanding of the background of a low-temperature detector, which is of interest to a large number of experiments.
understanding the origin and the spectral shape of the background, which is an important aspect of the CRESST analysis.
the understanding of the background in the CRESST detectors and the identification of possible background sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the background level in CRESST is understood, and the background model can be used to further reduce the level of background events.
we understand the spectra well enough to be confident in our ability to detect rare events.
the background in the CRESST experiment is well understood, with a few exceptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a good understanding of the background in our CaWO 4 detectors and we can explain all features of our spectra with known background sources.
the CRESST detectors are very stable and show a good long term performance.
the CRESST experiment is currently limited by a background of about 0.1 counts per day and keV energy interval.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the high level of background suppression in CRESST, the intrinsic background is still a significant component of the overall background level.
the background spectra are dominated by electron interactions in the detector material.
the background level in CRESST is well understood and can be further reduced by improving the radiopurity of the detector components.
